    Interim time zone guidance for Alberta, British Columbia, and Morocco
    Three time zone changes affect Windows devices in Alberta, British Columbia, and Morocco, with fixes releasing across September and October 2026. Alberta and affected Northwest Territories locations are permanently moving to UTC-6 on November 1, 2026. Most of British Columbia is permanently moving to UTC-7 on the same date. Morocco turned its clocks back one hour to UTC+0 on September 20, 2026. Microsoft recommends temporary workarounds for devices that can't be updated in time. For the workaround steps and full guidance for each region, visit the Daylight Saving Time & Time Zone Blog.

    Windows Deployment Services (WDS) deprecation in the next Windows Server release
    Microsoft plans to deprecate the Windows Deployment Services (WDS) server role beginning with the next release of Windows Server. This includes the inbox WDS role, WDS services, management tools, and interfaces, and WDS-provided Preboot Execution Environment (PXE) boot functionality. Begin planning your migration to alternatives. For example, Microsoft Configuration Manager provides a better, more flexible, and feature-rich experience for deploying Windows images. Learn more at Windows Deployment Services (WDS) deprecation in the next Windows Server release.

    (Updated) The September 2026 Windows non-security preview update is now available
    (Updated 9-22-2026: Added a note indicating the September 2026 non-security preview update is the final preview update for Windows 11, version 24H2.)

    The September 2026 non-security preview update is now available for Windows 11, versions 26H1, 25H2, and 24H2. Information about the contents of this update is available in the release notes, which are accessible from the Windows 11 update history page. For instructions on how to install this update on your home device, see the Update Windows article. To learn more about the different types of monthly quality updates, see Understanding Windows monthly updates. To stay informed about the latest updates and releases, follow @WindowsUpdate on X.
     
    Looking to explore upcoming features and improvements in Windows 11? Check the Windows roadmap. It includes what’s coming to the Windows Insider Program, what's gradually rolling out, and what's generally available.
     
    Highlights for the Windows 11, version 25H2 update:
    • You can now remap the Copilot key to function as the Right Ctrl or Context Menu key, helping preserve familiar keyboard shortcuts and accessibility workflows.
    • Camera roll backup in Settings helps eligible users protect their photos with OneDrive. You can turn on the feature from the Settings Home or Accounts page and finish setup on your phone using a QR code.
    • Windows now supports Emoji 17.0, adding new emoji such as distorted face, fight cloud, and hairy creature, and refreshing several existing designs including saluting face, goose, and lotus for better consistency across platforms. To insert them, press Windows key + Period (.) to open the emoji panel.
    • File Explorer now handles downloaded files more flexibly, with a new Preview anyway button for HTML files and automatic previews for non-HTML files such as PDFs, while Home remembers whether each section is expanded or collapsed and the reorganized Details pane shows cloud file thumbnails more reliably.
    • A new Open apps maximized setting automatically maximizes app windows as they open, whether you use a screen reader or magnification, work in tablet mode, or simply prefer a consistent full-screen workspace.
    Note: The September 2026 non-security preview update (KB5124010) is the final preview update for Windows 11, version 24H2. Supported editions of version 24H2 will continue to receive monthly security updates in accordance with their servicing lifecycle. To continue receiving non-security preview updates, please update to a newer version of Windows 11. As a reminder, Windows 11, version 24H2 Home and Pro editions reach end of support in October 2026.

    Note: With recent and upcoming Windows updates over the next few months, a limited number of consumer and business devices might experience one additional restart during installation. This one‑time restart occurs after a Secure Boot certificate update is applied as part of the Secure Boot update process.

    Intune: Windows Health Attestation Migration to Microsoft Azure Attestation
    If you manage Windows 11 devices via Microsoft Intune, a compliance-related change is planned for the first half of 2027. Windows Health Attestation compliance evaluation will automatically migrate from the current Device Health Attestation (DHA) service to Microsoft Azure Attestation (MAA). To prepare and avoid interruptions, review your organization’s network, firewall, proxy, and endpoint access configurations. Follow the instructions in Configure endpoints for Azure Attestation migration.

    60-Day Reminder: Windows 11, version 23H2 Enterprise and Education editions reach end of updates on November 10, 2026
    On November 10, 2026, Windows 11, version 23H2 Enterprise and Education editions will reach end of updates. The November 2026 Windows security update will be the last update available for these editions. After this date, devices running these editions will no longer receive monthly security and non-security preview updates containing protections from the latest security threats.

    To continue receiving monthly security and quality updates, we recommend updating eligible devices running Windows 11, version 23H2 Enterprise and Education editions to Windows 11, version 25H2. Windows 11, version 25H2 Enterprise and Education editions will continue to receive updates until October 11, 2028.

    For more information about product lifecycle dates, see Windows 11 release information and Lifecycle FAQ - Windows.

    Take Action: Out-of-band update released to address issues from the September 2026 Windows security update
    Microsoft has identified issues that affect some devices after installing the September 2026 Windows security update, released September 8, 2026. On affected devices, host folder shares might be unavailable in Hyper-V-based Linux virtual machines, Remote Desktop Services might stop responding, which can prevent new sessions from being created and can prevent local and remote sign-in, and some USB Audio Class 1.0 devices might fail in multichannel audio modes. 
     
    An out-of-band (OOB) update was released today, September 14, 2026, to address these issues. For most versions of Windows, these are cumulative updates that include all improvements from the September 2026 Windows security update released September 8, 2026, so you do not need to install any previous update first, except as noted below for hotpatch updates. 
     
    For Windows 11, versions 26H1, 25H2, and 24H2, this OOB update is a security update. It downloads and installs automatically from Windows Update and from Windows Update for Business in accordance with configured policies. It is also available from the Microsoft Update Catalog and syncs automatically with Windows Server Update Services (WSUS). 
     
    A corresponding hotpatch update is available from Windows Update for Windows 11, versions 25H2 and 24H2 for devices enrolled in hotpatch updates. Devices must have the September 2026 security update installed to receive this hotpatch update automatically. 
     
    The update for Windows 11, versions 26H1, 25H2, and 24H2 includes a security fix to address CVE-2026-62721. The update for Windows 11, version 26H1 also includes a security fix to address CVE-2026-85921.

    For Windows 11, version 23H2, and Windows 10, version 22H2 (ESU), this update is an optional non-security update. To install it, go to Settings > Windows Update, select Check for updates, and then select Download and install. It is also available from the Microsoft Update Catalog.  
     
    For complete guidance and installation instructions, see the relevant KB articles:

    • Windows 10 Enterprise LTSB 2016 and Windows Server 2016: KB5129239 
    • Windows Server 2012 R2: KB5129243 
    • Windows Server 2012: KB5129244

    30-Day Reminder: Windows 11, version 24H2 and Windows 10 LTSB 2016 reaching end of updates on October 13, 2026
    On October 13, 2026, Windows 11, version 24H2 Home and Pro editions, and Windows 10 Enterprise LTSB 2016 will reach end of updates. After this date, devices running these editions will no longer receive monthly security and non-security preview updates containing protections from the latest security threats.

    We recommend updating devices running Windows 11, version 24H2 Home and Pro editions to Windows 11, version 25H2 to continue receiving monthly security and quality updates. Enterprise and Education editions remain supported until October 12, 2027. For more information, see the How to get the Windows 11 2025 Update video.

    For devices running Windows 10 Enterprise LTSB 2016, we recommend updating to the latest Long-Term Servicing Channel (LTSC) release, Windows 11 Enterprise LTSC 2024. Extended Security Updates (ESU) are also available for organizations that need additional time to complete their transition.

    For more information about product lifecycle dates, see Windows 11 release information, Windows 10 release information, and Lifecycle FAQ - Windows.

    30-Day Reminder: AD FS DKM container ACL hardening begins in October 2026
    In October 2026, Windows updates will begin Enforcement mode for AD FS Distributed Key Manager (DKM) container ACL hardening, a change designed to address the elevation of privilege vulnerability documented in CVE-2026-56155. If your organization uses AD FS, review DKM container permissions during the remaining Audit mode period and address compatibility issues before enforcement begins.

    During Enforcement mode, supported versions of Windows Server will run remediation by default unless administrators explicitly opt out. Windows Server 2012 and Windows Server 2012 R2 still require manual remediation and will not be automatically remediated.

    For more details, see CVE-2026-56155: AD FS Distributed Key Manager container ACL hardening.

    30-Day Reminder: Windows Server 2022 will reach end of mainstream support on October 13, 2026
    On October 13, 2026, Windows Server 2022 will reach end of mainstream support. The October 2026 security update will be the last mainstream support update available for this version. After this date, Windows Server 2022 will transition to extended support, which includes security updates at no additional cost, and will continue to receive monthly security updates through October 14, 2031. For more information, see the Fixed Lifecycle Policy.

    Hotpatch update support for Windows Server 2022 Datacenter: Azure Edition has been extended through October 2027. Devices enrolled in Hotpatch updates will continue to receive monthly security updates without requiring a restart. To learn more, see the Windows Server 2022 lifecycle page.

    Windows Server 2025 is now the latest Long-Term Servicing Channel (LTSC) release for Windows Server. To help keep your environment protected and supported, plan to upgrade to Windows Server 2025 for full mainstream support. To download a free 180-day evaluation, visit the Microsoft Evaluation Center. Evaluate upgrade options and begin deployment testing early to help ensure a smooth transition.

    For detailed lifecycle dates, see the Windows Server 2022 lifecycle page. For servicing timelines and related resources, see Windows Server release information, Lifecycle FAQ - Windows Server, and Microsoft Lifecycle Policy search tool.

    Highlights for the Windows 11, version 25H2 update:
    • This security update includes improvements that were part of update KB5120998 (released August 27, 2026).
    • This update expands high confidence device targeting data, increasing coverage of devices eligible to automatically receive new Secure Boot certificates. Devices receive the new certificates only after demonstrating sufficient successful update signals, maintaining a controlled and phased rollout.
    • This update makes quality improvements to the servicing stack, which is the component that installs Windows updates.
